mcat_description.short: Modular buildings are factory-manufactured prefabricated structures assembled on-site from individual modules, sold as complete units or turnkey building systems for residential, commercial, and industrial applications.
mcat_description.long: Modular buildings are engineered structures where individual modules — complete with walls, floors, roofing, and pre-installed services — are manufactured in a controlled factory environment and transported to site for rapid assembly. In the Indian market, they span a wide range from portable steel-frame cabins and site offices to multi-storey permanent residential and commercial buildings, with structural systems including steel frame, sandwich panel (PUF/EPS/rock wool core), prefabricated concrete, and hybrid composite construction. Key Indian standards governing design and erection include IS 15916:2011 (prefabricated concrete systems) and IS 15917:2010 (mixed/composite construction), with compliance also required under the National Building Code of India and local municipal regulations. Buyers value modular buildings for speed of deployment, cost predictability, relocatability, and scalability — with construction timelines reduced by 30–50% versus conventional RCC methods.

market_context: The Indian modular construction market is a fast-growing segment of the prefabricated structures industry, driven by urbanisation, infrastructure development, and demand for faster, cost-predictable construction. Two independent market research sources (Grand View Research and IMARC Group) confirm strong growth: the market was valued at approximately USD 3.9 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach USD 8.3 billion by 2033 at a CAGR of approximately 9.9%. Permanent modular construction is the dominant segment by revenue (85.2% share in 2025), though relocatable/portable structures remain the most visible product type on B2B platforms. Key structural systems in the Indian market include steel-frame sandwich panel buildings (PUF/EPS/rock wool core), prefabricated concrete systems (governed by IS 15916:2011), mixed/composite construction (IS 15917:2010), and hybrid systems combining steel frames with precast concrete. Tata Steel's Nest-In (MobiNest) is a prominent branded player in the portable cabin and site office segment; other active manufacturers include MODULI, Pressmach, Wedge India, and KMS Technologies. Buyers in India distinguish between relocatable structures (portable cabins, site offices, labour camps — typically steel frame, lightweight) and permanent modular buildings (residential, commercial, institutional — heavier construction, BIS/NBC compliant). The Google keyword signal 'prefabricated room on terrace' (top impression-driving query) indicates a significant residential extension sub-segment unique to the Indian market. Compliance requirements include BIS codes (IS 15916, IS 15917), National Building Code of India, local municipal building permits, and fire safety clearances.
